subject: C14
required_fixes: R6 — The body-ownership guard rejects exclusively owned JSON body files as schemas. project.rs:292/:449 adds every .json/.yaml/.yml file to Catalog.schemas, including request body sidecars. document.rs:785 then includes all those candidates in project_files; shared() matches the body file against itself, and plan():721 returns sharedBody on any body edit. A valid request with body="items/post.body.json" therefore cannot save its own changed JSON payload even when no other request or schema association owns it. This also affects all 53 nonempty JSON bodies in the built-in catalogue: scm.rs:96 deliberately generates .body.json sidecars. The ownership fixture's positive control uses own.body.txt and misses this regression. Distinguish schema candidates from actual conflicting ownership/roles rather than blocking solely by extension. Acceptance: production-interface tests save and reopen an exclusively owned JSON body and a representative built-in JSON request, with metadata and unrelated files preserved; retain refusals for actual shared bodies, case/normalization aliases, metadata files and genuinely conflicting schema ownership.
limitations: Read-only review: no implementation files were changed, no application/endpoints were launched, and no credentials were accessed. R6 is established by tracing production discovery, ownership and Save code and inspecting catalogue metadata; the proposed negative/positive Rust fixtures were not newly executed by this reviewer.
